scope: Synthetic Chromium inline handwriting linked to native PDF text annotations, using the real Python worker and host storage.
checks: trusted pen creates a standard text-bound highlight
sidebar handwriting button spans its action row with an unobstructed 44-pixel target
active handwriting and finish controls retain unobstructed 44-pixel targets
sidebar handwriting toggle keeps PDF visible without a separate board
pause autosaves visible PDF circle as native ink bound to the highlight
another page cannot acquire handwriting belonging to the selected highlight
touch input does not create linked handwriting
same toggle flushes mouse-fallback strokes and restores the prior text tool
normal text markup works immediately after leaving linked handwriting
unknown save acknowledgement keeps exact linked draft and locks edits
reload restores parent binding and same retry ID without duplicate ink
failed exit retains selected highlight and unsaved strokes
explicit retry saves a refused batch and then permits exit
existing attachment-based note remains accessible and unchanged
linked ink belongs under its parent instead of creating independent sidebar cards
export and fresh import recover native ink relationships and legacy attachment from PDF alone
confirmed linked strokes reopen in the reading page
600-pixel viewport keeps full-row handwriting and enlarged finish controls visible with pending retry
dark-theme inactive handwriting action preserves readable contrast and visible click targets
original bytes unchanged with no browser errors or external model requests
limitations: Physical Apple Pencil, Sidecar and Safari were not exercised.
Reload recovery covers completed strokes acknowledged by host storage; abrupt termination of unfinished or unacknowledged writes is not guaranteed.
Fixed-width ink; no pressure or iPadOS palm rejection claim.
